evidence.quote: Ex archetypo enim perantiquo (Ω) apographa ante saeculum nonum facta esse statuamus duo, x et y, ex y rursus duo, z et w. Omnia haec apographa passa iam sunt manus interpolatorum
Et primum quidem ad x referimus libros V et P quam maxime affines.
[stemma diagram printed here; OCR keeps only fragments 'GM' and 'A B'] Ex quibus codices Ω x y z w α quos supponimus periisse dictum est.
Ex w autem et z multi et Π pendet, ita tamen, ut etiam ex x non pauca assumpserit ... et magis etiam interpolatus α cum filiis A et B. Porro P multa ex x habet
Exempli z tria apographa adhibui, R, E, C.
Stirpes autem duae ex archetypo Ω germinaverant, x et y; ex y rursus duae, z et w; ad x et z et w accedebant libri duplicis naturae ... quales sunt P et Π.

texts.notes: Birt prints a stemma (p. CIII; Ω > x, y; y > z, w; w > α > A, B) but calls it a 'magis umbratilem adumbrationem' and says P (x + w) and Π (w + z, some x) are mixed; P is placed under x, Π under y here. One stemma covers carmina maiora and the minora corpusculum, whose witnesses differ (R, G, M, J, E only in the minora). Check the sigla in the dMGH images: the OCR conspectus gives the Ambrosianus as J and the Vicentina as A, and E means different things in the two sections.

evidence.quote: Priore autem tempore id acciderat ut duae maxime carminis sive recensiones sive conformationes existerent, plenior altera, altera decurtata.
Sed ad has duas classis etiam media in paucis tantum libris servata accedit ... quibus omnibus indiciis huius mediae classis cum altera nexum artissimum esse evincitur
Cum his libris classis secundae libri tertiae classis pauci arte cohaerent qui quidem sunt hi: III: Musei Britannici 6042 (D). Antverpiensis III 59 (W)
I 216 S et W et AC Curarum secreta tibi cytharea, contra recte et [sigla garbled] ...: Curarum citarea tibi secreta: ita miscentur familiae!

texts.notes: Three classes: I (Ia/Ib: F, V, S), II (C, A, B), III ('media': D, W). Birt names two ancient forms, the full one (I) and the shortened one (II), and ties class III closely to II, so the top is read as I vs II+III. It could also be read as three coordinate classes. He documents agreements of single codices across all three classes ('ita miscentur familiae'). The A/B shelfmarks are inconsistent between the OCR conspectus and the preface, so check them on the page images.

evidence.quote: Qui libri ut solitam interpolationis libidinem passi sunt omnes, libros tamen BRW paullo meliores atque tales esse demonstrabo, ut in iis propemodum editor et emendator carminis acquiescere possit
Et primum libri L F P T Vo et l, cum unusquisque suos errores multifarios commiserint, nullam paene veram et genuinam lectionem tradidere quae non in illis quoque ... scripta sit

texts.notes: Birt ranks the witnesses as BRW better and LFPT (plus Vo, l) worse, and lists BRW agreements, but he states no derivation, class or archetype. The pairing BRW vs LFPT could be read as a two-group division, so check whether that counts as a stated filiation. Witnesses also agree across the two groups ('concinant vel succinant').
